title: The Elder Scrolls Began as a Gladiator Game Called Arena
hook: The first Elder Scrolls game is called Arena because in 1993 it really was a gladiator tournament game, and the boxes were printed before it turned into an RPG. This week Bethesda finally named The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Which Elder Scrolls did you play first? Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know The Elder Scrolls started out as a gladiator game, and that is the only reason the first one is called Arena? Back in 1993, a small team at Bethesda Softworks was building a game about teams of fighters battling through tournaments. Designer Ted Peterson has said the tournaments mattered less and less as work went on. The team kept adding towns, dungeons and quests until the project turned into a massive role playing game. Peterson says the advertising was already done and the boxes already printed with the name Arena, so the name stayed. The writers even explained it inside the story by giving the Empire itself the nickname the Arena. The game missed Christmas of 1993 and finally shipped on March twenty fifth, 1994, for MS DOS. Only a few thousand copies went out at first, and some stores cancelled their orders. Word of mouth slowly turned it into a hit, and Bethesda has been making Elder Scrolls games ever since. This week, Bethesda marked forty years with an anniversary video, and it ended with a surprise. The Elder Scrolls Six finally has a name, Sentinel, and it is set in Hammerfell. There is still no release date. Which Elder Scrolls game did you play first? Follow for more gaming history.
